playbook_name: Atlas OS Supreme — Operational Playbook v1.0
governing_principle: CEO Super Agent holds supreme operational authority. Escalation to Project Owner is reserved for strategic decisions only.

task_lifecycle.description: Every task flows through 7 stages from inception to closure

actions: Agents continuously monitor their domains for opportunities, risks, and improvements
External inputs (market shifts, user feedback, system alerts) are auto-captured
Internal inputs (bottlenecks, inefficiencies, knowledge gaps) are self-reported
Every intake is tagged with: source, urgency, estimated impact, suggested owner
stages.sla: Intake processed within 1 hour of detection

actions: CEO reviews all ORTTs during daily triage (0600 UTC)
Classification: Strategic (escalate to owner), Operational (auto-route), Tactical (department-level)
Strategic decisions require Project Owner approval per escalation matrix
Operational decisions are auto-assigned by CEO based on agent capacity, expertise, and workload
Tactical decisions are delegated to Department Chiefs for sub-assignment
stages.sla: Triage complete within 4 hours of intake

actions: Assigned agent creates Task Plan: scope, approach, dependencies, risks, success criteria
Dependencies are auto-notified and must acknowledge within 2 hours
If dependencies conflict, Escalation Manager mediates; unresolved conflicts go to CEO
Cross-department tasks trigger a Coordination Sync with all affected Department Chiefs
Plan is stored in organizational memory before execution begins
stages.output: Approved Task Plan with Dependency Acknowledgments
stages.sla: Planning complete within 8 hours of assignment

actions: Agent executes task using standard operating procedures from organizational memory
Progress is logged in real-time to the Task Tracker
Blockers are reported immediately; blockers >2 hours trigger automatic escalation
Agents may request assistance from Knowledge Base or other agents without CEO involvement
All code, documents, and artifacts are versioned and linked to the task ticket
stages.sla: Per task estimate; blockers escalated within 2 hours

actions: Automated quality gates run first: tests, linting, security scans, performance benchmarks
Peer review by at least one agent from a different sub-team
Department Chief validates alignment with department strategy and standards
Cross-department work requires sign-off from all affected Department Chiefs
Quality failures loop back to T4 with specific remediation instructions
stages.output: Quality Approval Stamp or Remediation Request
stages.sla: Review complete within 12 hours of submission

actions: Self-Learning Loop auto-triggers upon task closure
Lessons Learned, Best Practices, Reusable Components, and Architecture Improvements are extracted
Memory Architect indexes new knowledge into the organizational memory graph
Knowledge Graph Agent updates entity and relationship mappings
All future agents automatically inherit this knowledge through retrieval-augmented context
stages.sla: Knowledge capture complete within 24 hours of closure

actions: Task officially closed with final metrics: time, cost, quality, business impact
KPIs for all involved agents are updated
Success/failure patterns are analyzed by Model Evaluation Agent
CEO reviews weekly closure reports for organizational optimization opportunities
Exceptional work triggers agent evolution (capability upgrade or specialization split)
stages.sla: Closure metrics published within 4 hours of T6 completion

real_time.response_sla: < 5 minutes for critical; < 30 minutes for high priority

daily.response_sla: < 2 hours for operational; < 4 hours for tactical

weekly.response_sla: < 24 hours for decisions; < 48 hours for feedback

monthly.response_sla: < 1 week for strategic decisions; < 2 weeks for implementation plans

level_1.trigger: Task blockers, resource conflicts, scope ambiguity

level_2.trigger: Cross-department conflicts, budget overruns >$10K, quality failures, SLA breaches
level_2.resolution_authority: Department reorganization, budget approval up to $50K, process changes, agent retraining

level_3.trigger: Public launch, legal commitments, external payments >$100K, irreversible production changes, business partnerships, material business changes
level_3.resolution_authority: Final approval on all strategic decisions with material business impact

level_4.trigger: Critical security breach, ethics violation, regulatory enforcement, existential business risk
level_4.resolution_authority: Emergency powers: system shutdown, legal hold, public communication, executive override

cross_department_tasks.protocol: When a task spans >1 department, a Coordination Lead is appointed (usually the agent from the department with the largest scope)
steps: Coordination Lead creates a Unified Task Plan with inputs/outputs from each department
Each Department Chief assigns their contributing agents and confirms capacity
Daily cross-department syncs are mandatory until task completes
Conflicts are resolved by Escalation Manager; unresolved conflicts escalate to CEO
Final integration is owned by the Coordination Lead with QA from all departments

shared_resources.protocol: All shared resources (compute, data, tools, personnel) are managed by Resource Allocation Agent
rules: Resource requests are submitted via the Resource Allocation Queue
Priority scoring: Strategic (10x) > Revenue-impacting (5x) > Operational (2x) > Maintenance (1x)
Conflicts are resolved by priority score; ties broken by CEO decision
All resource usage is logged and optimized by Cost Optimization Agent monthly

knowledge_sharing.protocol: Knowledge is shared through the organizational memory system, not ad-hoc
rules: All agents query organizational memory before starting a new task
Agents must document discoveries in standard format before task closure
Weekly Knowledge Syncs highlight cross-cutting insights
Memory Architect ensures knowledge is findable within 3 queries
Redundant work detected by Automation Coordination triggers agent retraining

conflict_resolution.principle: Conflicts are resolved by data and mission alignment, not hierarchy alone
process: Step 1: Conflicting agents present their positions with supporting data to Escalation Manager
Step 2: Escalation Manager assesses alignment with organizational mission and global rules
Step 3: If positions are equally valid, a rapid A/B test or prototype is built to validate
Step 4: If still unresolved, CEO Super Agent makes final decision with documented rationale
Step 5: Losing position is archived in organizational memory with reasoning (no blame, only learning)

ceo_autonomous: Technical architecture changes within approved frameworks
requires_owner_approval: Public product launch or major version release
Irreversible production changes (data migrations, platform switches)
Changes that materially affect revenue, valuation, or brand
